assertions_evaluated.text: AMENDED after grading (see grading.json note): the primary expired-token-rejection finding correctly applies the risk-to-evidence-matrix's High-risk bar, which requires a behavior test/manual trial PLUS a distinct security/adversarial check for a trust-boundary change -- since only one behavior test covered one scenario, 'weak' (not 'adequate') is the textually correct classification. The original assertion here expected 'adequate'; that expectation was miscalibrated against the skill's own written risk matrix, not a skill defect.
assertions_evaluated.evidence: Baseline substantively pushes toward the same conclusion in unstructured prose -- 'It doesn't yet prove the boundary is exactly right, that failure modes degrade safely (401, not 500 or fail-open), or that adjacent invalid-token handling wasn't disturbed... #1 (boundary) and #2 (malformed claim / fail-open vs. fail-closed) are the two I'd treat as non-optional before calling this done -- those are the classic places where "looks right, passes the test I wrote" hides a real security gap' -- but it never applies the formal 'weak' classification label, never names a risk-to-evidence-matrix, and never frames the gap as 'one behavior test is not enough evidence for a High-risk trust-boundary change' -- it argues from general auth-testing experience (boundary/edge-case coverage), not from a risk-proportionate evidence bar.

assertions_evaluated.text: The regression-suite finding and the valid-token manual-trial finding are each separately classified 'adequate' at their own (Medium) risk level, distinct from the primary fix's own (High) risk level
assertions_evaluated.evidence: Baseline lists both under a single undifferentiated 'What's covered well' bullet list -- 'Regression check against existing suite (12 tests) passing' and 'One manual positive check (valid token -> still works)' -- with no risk-tier language (no 'Medium risk', no explicit 'adequate' verdict) and no distinction from the primary finding's own risk level; it never separates these into their own lower-risk adequacy tier at all.
